description: A published package carries no lockfile, so the range in its manifest is what a consumer installs against. The range is therefore a claim about what the package accepts to run, and 'bump' moves its floor with the update rather than leaving a floor nobody would run behind.

packageRules.description: A development tool reaches no consumer tree, so an exact version costs no duplication and buys an identical toolchain on every machine and every run.
The toolchain moves as one piece, so the gate judges it as one piece and a repository receives one pull request rather than six.

The types describe the oldest node these servers accept. Typing against a newer line lets an API that does not exist there compile clean and fail at the version the package tells its callers to run. This bound moves with the floor.
The declaration bundler inside tsup reads an internal of the compiler that the 7 line no longer exposes, and the build dies after the JavaScript. Lift this bound when tsup builds against that line.
The image is built on the node line these servers ask for. This bound moves with the floor.
A server that another server reads carries behaviour rather than tooling, so it travels in its own pull request and its changelog is read.
